Abstract
Hamiltonian simulation using product formulas is arguably the most straightforward and practical
approach for algorithmic simulation of a quantum system’s dynamics on a quantum computer. Here we
present corrected product formulas (CPFs), a variation of product formulas achieved by injecting auxiliary
terms called correctors into standard product formulas. We establish several correctors that greatly improve
the accuracy of standard product formulas for simulating Hamiltonians comprised of two partitions that
can be exactly simulated, a common feature of lattice Hamiltonians, while only adding a small additive
or multiplicative factor to the simulation cost. We show that correctors are particularly advantageous for
perturbed systems, where one partition has a relatively small norm compared to the other, as they allow the

methods.value: Injecting auxiliary terms called correctors into standard product formulas to create CPFs, establishing several correctors that greatly improve the accuracy of standard product formulas while only adding a small additive or multiplicative factor to the simulation cost.

problems.value: Developing efficient methods for simulating Hamiltonian evolution on quantum computers, particularly for systems with a Hamiltonian of the form H = A + αB where A and B have comparable norms and can be exactly simulated.

hypotheses.value: Corrected product formulas (CPFs) can significantly improve the accuracy of standard product formulas for simulating Hamiltonians comprised of two partitions that can be exactly simulated.

evidence.value: Numerical simulations for various lattice Hamiltonians demonstrate that the theoretical performance of CPFs matches or exceeds the empirical performance of standard product formulas.

conclusions.value: CPFs are a valuable algorithmic tool for early fault-tolerant quantum computers with limited computing resources, offering significant improvements in simulation accuracy and efficiency.
